title: Pointwise normalized comparison of integral tower generators
statement:
The Lean theorem `integralInverseSystem_unit_normalization_components` has the following statement:

theorem integralInverseSystem_unit_normalization_components (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (I : ∀ n : ℕ, SheafOfModules.AlgebraicInverseImage (Scheme.proEtaleSheafInverseImage f (Type (u + 1))) ((Rrings l Y).obj (Opposite.op n)) ((Rrings l X).obj (Opposite.op n))) (P : WeilConjectures.SemilinearSections.OrdinaryInverseSystem.{u + 1, u, u + 1} (Scheme.ProEt.topology Y) (fun n ↦ (Rrings l Y).obj (Opposite.op n)) (fun n ↦ (Rrings l Y).map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (Scheme.proEtaleSheafInverseImage f (Type (u + 1))) (fun n ↦ (Rrings l X).obj (Opposite.op n)) (fun n ↦ (Rrings l X).map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) I) (FY : Forget Y (Rrings l Y)) (FX : Forget X (Rrings l X)) (e : FY.F ⋙ abPull f ≅ P.pull ⋙ FX.F) : ∃ i : P.pull.obj (coefficient Y (Rrings l Y)) ≅ coefficient X (Rrings l X), ∀ (n : ℕ) (U : X.ProEtᵒᵖ) (x : (((abPull f).obj (integers Y)).obj (op n)).obj.obj U), (((((abPull f).map (integerGenerator Y (Rrings l Y) FY)) ≫ e.hom.app (coefficient Y (Rrings l Y))) ≫ FX.F.map i.hom).app (op n)).hom.app U x = ((integerPull f ≫ integerGenerator X (Rrings l X) FX).app (op n)).hom.app U x

source.place: Paragraph (2): integral reduction to (Z/ell^(n+1))_n; the coefficient-unit comparison is checked on constant integer sections.

proof.text: Every additive sheaf map between modules over the constant residue ring is linear by lem-pur-torsion-sheaf-constant-module, after restriction along purTwistFiniteRingIso. Use Forget.sections, restrictions, transitions and morphisms to transport an additive tower morphism to a presheaf morphism. The levelwise linearity makes its components module morphisms. Naturality is inherited from the additive tower map; Forget.morphisms proves that this is a lift. The same section formulas give faithfulness, so additive tower isomorphisms lift to module-system isomorphisms.
proof.elementary: Explicit constructions, transport of equalities, and Mathlib naturality and sheafification universal properties.

proof.text: Identify the forgotten coefficient system with the underlying additive ring tower using Forget.sections and the restriction and transition equations. Apply Mathlib constantCommuteCompose for the composite forgetting functor CommRingCat to RingCat to AddCommGrpCat. Naturality for each residue quotient identifies this with the tower of constant additive residue groups.
proof.elementary: Explicit constructions, transport of equalities, and Mathlib naturality and sheafification universal properties.

proof.text: The canonical inverse-image map of an additive constant sheaf is an isomorphism: identify it with the unique comparison between two left adjoints to sections over the terminal object. Naturality in additive coefficient homomorphisms assembles these maps into an isomorphism of the residue towers. Conjugate by the preceding coefficient identifications to obtain the canonical abelian coefficient comparison.
proof.elementary: Explicit constructions, transport of equalities, and Mathlib naturality and sheafification universal properties.

proof.text: The defining section formula of integerGenerator and constantCommuteCompose compatibility with toSheafify show that integerGenerator followed by the coefficient identification is constantSheaf.map of the integer quotient. Naturality of the canonical constant-sheaf comparison for this quotient gives the normalized integer equation. Use sheafify_hom_ext to extend the calculation on constant integer generators to all sections.
proof.elementary: Explicit constructions, transport of equalities, and Mathlib naturality and sheafification universal properties.

proof.text: Conjugate the canonical abelian coefficient comparison by the inverse of the given component of e. Lift this isomorphism through the fully faithful forgetting functor constructed in the first step. Its image is the conjugated comparison; composition with e cancels the inverse. Substitute the normalized integer equation and evaluate at n, U and x.
proof.elementary: Explicit constructions, transport of equalities, and Mathlib naturality and sheafification universal properties.
